task_spec.title: Simulation Task
task_spec.description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption time series.

metrics.description: Coefficient of determination between simulated and observed adoption levels.

metrics.description: Absolute difference in days between observed peak adoption and simulated peak adoption.

validation_criteria.name: Convergence_criterion
validation_criteria.description: Calibration terminates when improvement in the target metric across iterations falls below a tolerance for N successive iterations.

validation_criteria.name: Parameter_bounds_respected
validation_criteria.description: All calibrated parameters remain within specified prior bounds.

validation_criteria.name: Goodness_of_fit_threshold
validation_criteria.description: Accept calibrated model if target metric (e.g., RMSE_of_adoption) is below a pre-specified threshold.

validation_criteria.name: Stability_check
validation_criteria.description: Simulated adoption does not exhibit unrealistic oscillations or divergence under small perturbations.

key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous risk perception
key_patterns.description: risk_perception is continuous on [0,1] with agent-to-agent variability; likely skewed and heterogeneous across age_group and occupation.
key_patterns.relevance: Sets heterogeneous baseline propensity to adopt masks and moderates sensitivity to peer influence.

key_patterns.name: Layered multiplex network
key_patterns.description: Three layers (family, work_school, community) with differing contact intensity and clustering; family is dense and small, work/school medium, community broader and sparser.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence weights and contact rates are needed to model diffusion accurately.

key_patterns.name: Demographic homophily
key_patterns.description: Edges cluster by age_group and occupation, especially in work_school; family ties also align by age cohorts.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily can slow or accelerate diffusion within subgroups; informs layer weights and mixing matrices.

key_patterns.name: Initial condition heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: Day 0 wearing_mask and received_info vary across agents; seeds are not uniform and likely clustered in certain layers/subgroups.
key_patterns.relevance: Accurate initialization is critical for matching early adoption trajectory and peak timing.

key_patterns.name: Information precedes behavior
key_patterns.description: Transitions to wearing_mask are more frequent among agents with received_info=true in prior timestep.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports a two-stage mechanism: info diffusion raises adoption propensity; informs causal pathway parameters.

key_patterns.name: Peer spillovers
key_patterns.description: Adoption probability increases with the fraction of masked neighbors (within- and cross-layer effects).
key_patterns.relevance: Quantifies social influence coefficients and layer weights for the behavior update rule.

key_patterns.name: Behavioral persistence (habit/inertia)
key_patterns.description: P(wear_t+1 | wear_t=1) > P(wear_t+1 | wear_t=0), and dis-adoption is relatively rare but non-zero.
key_patterns.relevance: Requires inclusion of persistence/decay parameters to match plateau and final adoption levels.

key_patterns.name: S-curve aggregate adoption
key_patterns.description: Population-level wearing_mask shows sigmoidal growth, a peak/plateau, and possible slight decline.
key_patterns.relevance: Guides choice of functional forms (threshold/probit) and calibration targets for RMSE/MAE/R2 and peak timing.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: Continuous distribution on [0,1]; Beta family is appropriate.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(a,b) via MLE on risk_perception; store (a_hat, b_hat) and subgroup fits by age_group and occupation.

key_distributions.name: Degree distributions by layer
key_distributions.description: Per-layer node degrees: family (small mean, low variance), work_school (moderate, near-Poisson within groups), community (right-skewed/heavy-tailed).
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L: mean_degree_L, var_degree_L, tail_index_L (if heavy-tailed), and degree assortativity.

key_distributions.name: Clustering and path lengths
key_distributions.description: High clustering in family, moderate in work/school, low in community; small-world path lengths.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L: global_clustering_L, avg_path_length_L; multiplex overlap coefficient.

key_distributions.name: State transition probabilities
key_distributions.description: Daily Markov transitions for wearing_mask and received_info.
key_distributions.parameters: P11 = P(wear_t+1=1|wear_t=1), P01 = P(wear_t+1=1|wear_t=0); similarly for info: Q11, Q01; conditional on info_t.

key_distributions.name: Peer influence response
key_distributions.description: Logistic response of adoption to neighbors' masked fraction and info exposure.
key_distributions.parameters: Logit coefficients: beta0 (intercept), beta_peer_family, beta_peer_work, beta_peer_comm, beta_info, beta_risk, interactions (optional).

key_distributions.name: Homophily/mixing
key_distributions.description: Within- and between-group tie frequencies by age_group and occupation.
key_distributions.parameters: Mixing matrices M_age and M_occ; compute within-group edge fraction and assortativity r.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception associates with higher baseline adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via logistic regression coefficient beta_risk; expect positive and significant.

key_relationships.relationship: Information exposure at time t increases the probability of adopting at t+1.
key_relationships.strength: Effect size beta_info; compare P01 with and without info; expect substantial uplift.

key_relationships.relationship: Adoption probability increases with masked neighbors’ fraction; layer-specific slopes.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate beta_peer_family > beta_peer_work > beta_peer_comm; decreasing with social distance.

key_relationships.relationship: Occupation categories correlate with work/school layer degree (e.g., students high within school).
key_relationships.strength: Medium to strong; quantify via ANOVA or regression on degree.
Moderate; fit separate Beta parameters per age_group and test differences.

initial_mask_state_distribution.value: Use day=0 wearing_mask by agent from agent_daily_states.csv; if missing, sample by subgroup from observed day=0 rates.
initial_mask_state_distribution.notes: Preserve observed clustering by seeding info/mask in same agents if both available.

initial_info_state_distribution.value: Use day=0 received_info by agent; fallback to subgroup-specific rates.
initial_info_state_distribution.notes: If only aggregate known, assign via degree-proportional seeding to match observed info coverage.

risk_perception_distribution.value: Beta(a_hat,b_hat) fitted to risk_perception; stratify by age_group and occupation if significantly different.
risk_perception_distribution.notes: Normalize values to [0,1]; winsorize outliers if any.

layer_graphs.value: Construct three undirected simple graphs (family, work_school, community); enforce symmetric edges and remove duplicates.
layer_graphs.notes: Validate node set equals agent_attributes IDs; drop/isolate agents not present in attributes.

layer_contact_weights.value: w_family >= w_work_school >= w_community; initialize as proportional to observed adoption elasticity by layer from regression, then calibrate.
layer_contact_weights.source: Derived from peer-effect regression using agent_daily_states + network
layer_contact_weights.notes: Normalize weights to sum to 1 for interpretability.

mixing_matrices.value: M_age and M_occ computed from edge cross-tabs; use to generate synthetic ties for missing edges and to analyze homophily.
mixing_matrices.notes: Assortativity r_age and r_occ to be reported and used in sensitivity tests.

info_transmission_rate_per_contact.value: Estimate per-layer rates lambda_info_L via discrete-time hazard: Pr(info_t+1=1 | info_t=0, contact with informed neighbors); distinct for family/work/community.
info_transmission_rate_per_contact.notes: Use complementary log-log link for rare events; regularize to avoid overfitting.

exogenous_info_inflow.value: Background probability phi_info(t) capturing mass media; estimate from info incidence unexplained by neighbors.
exogenous_info_inflow.notes: Model as time-varying spline or piecewise constant.

adoption_logit_intercept.value: beta0 estimated from logistic regression of wear_t+1 on covariates when neighbor influence is zero.
adoption_logit_intercept.notes: Include day fixed effects if exogenous shocks exist.

peer_influence_coefficients.value: beta_peer_family, beta_peer_work, beta_peer_comm from logistic regression using layer-specific neighbor mask fractions.
peer_influence_coefficients.notes: Standardize neighbor fractions; consider random slopes by occupation.

risk_perception_effect.value: beta_risk linking risk_perception to adoption propensity (logit scale).

information_effect_on_adoption.notes: Optionally lagged effects over multiple days.

habit_persistence.value: P11 = Pr(wear_t+1=1|wear_t=1) estimated directly; include as additive bias or as separate coefficient.
habit_persistence.notes: Model both persistence and disadoption P10 to capture hysteresis.

disadoption_rate.value: P10 = Pr(wear_t+1=0|wear_t=1) estimated from transitions; may depend on neighbor fraction and info decay.
disadoption_rate.notes: Include penalty for rapid churn to match plateau.

adoption_threshold_distribution.value: If using threshold model, fit threshold ~ Beta or Normal on latent scale using observed switch points vs neighbor fractions.
adoption_threshold_distribution.notes: Alternative to logistic; choose one mechanism to avoid identifiability issues.

time_step_days.notes: Discrete daily updates with synchronous or staggered layer updates.

update_scheme.value: Synchronous daily updates; compute info first, then behavior.
update_scheme.source: Design choice informed by temporal precedence of info

adoption_aggregation.value: Compute daily population adoption and subgroup adoption (by age_group, occupation).
adoption_aggregation.notes: These series feed RMSE/MAE/R2, peak timing, and final gap metrics.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Stage 1: Estimate directly observable parameters from data (P11, P01, P10; beta_risk; beta_info; initial states; Beta(a,b) for risk_perception; per-layer degree stats and mixing). Stage 2: Fit social influence and layer weights via logistic regression of wear_t+1 on lagged neighbor mask fractions by layer, info_t, risk_perception, and persistence term, with agent random effects if feasible. Stage 3: Run the multi-agent simulation using estimated parameters as priors and calibrate remaining free parameters (e.g., exogenous info inflow, layer weights fine-tuning, disadoption modifiers) to minimize a composite loss over RMSE_of_adoption, MAE_of_adoption, 1-R2_of_adoption, Peak_timing_error_days, and Final_adoption_gap. Use Bayesian optimization or CMA-ES with k-fold time-block cross-validation; constrain parameters to plausible ranges; regularize to avoid overfitting.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out the final segment of the time series for validation; compare simulated vs observed adoption on the held-out days using all metrics. Additionally validate subgroup adoption curves (age_group, occupation) and sensitivity to network perturbations. Check that simulated peak timing and plateau levels are within tolerance. Perform posterior predictive checks or parametric bootstrap to quantify uncertainty bands around simulated adoption.
key_variables_to_calibrate: noise/temperature in decision rule (e.g., logit scale parameter)

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Data structure and type:
  - Flat CSV table; one row per agent.
  - Primary key: agent_id (integer, unique).
  - Columns include categorical and continuous attributes; no nested structures.

- Column meanings:
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an agent; used to join with network edges or other tables.
  - age_group: Categorical demographic bucket (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age); informs demographic heterogeneity.
  - occupation: Categorical role (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); proxies context/layer (school, workplace, community) and contact patterns.
  - risk_perception: Continuous value in [0,1] representing agent’s perceived risk of infection/illness; higher implies greater baseline propensity to adopt masks.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No explicit relationships in this file; relationships occur across agents via a separate social network/edges dataset.
  - Attributes can induce homophily or layered contacts (e.g., students more connected within school layer; white/blue collar within workplaces).

- How this data informs the simulation:
  - Agent initialization: Each row creates an agent with demographic attributes and an initial risk_perception state.
  - Behavior model:
    - risk_perception sets baseline mask adoption probability and sensitivity to peer influence or public signals.
    - age_group and occupation modulate:
      - Contact rates and layers (school, workplace, community).
      - Exposure to norms (e.g., student clusters) and policy effects (e.g., workplace mandates).
      - Potential heterogeneity in compliance thresholds and behavior change rates.
  - Network dynamics:
    - Use age_group/occupation to structure multilayer networks and homophilous ties; agent_id links to edge lists.
  - Calibration/segmentation:
    - Stratify outcomes and parameter tuning by age_group/occupation; ensure risk_perception is normalized and handle missing values before simulation.

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object (dictionary) where each entry represents one agent in a social network.
  - Top-level keys are agent IDs (strings that map to integer IDs); values are nested objects.

- Meaning of keys or columns:
  - Top-level key (e.g., "0", "1", "2"): unique agent identifier.
  - Nested keys:
    - family: list of agent IDs connected via family ties.
    - work_school: list of agent IDs connected via work or school ties.
    - community: list of agent IDs connected via broader community ties.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Each nested list is an adjacency list for a specific layer of a multiplex social network.
  - Edges are unweighted by default and may be implicitly undirected (verify or enforce symmetry during preprocessing).
  - Agent IDs in lists are integers; normalize top-level string IDs to integers for consistency.
  - Expect possible empty lists; handle duplicates and missing agents robustly.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Entities: create one agent per ID with state variables (e.g., mask_wearing: bool/prob, propensity/threshold, compliance, influence susceptibility).
  - Network: build three parallel graphs (family, work_school, community) or a single multiplex graph with labeled edges.
  - Dynamics: at each timestep, compute influence on an agent from neighbors, optionally weighting layers differently (e.g., family > work_school > community) and using rules like threshold, probabilistic contagion, or reinforcement.
  - Scheduling: sample interactions per layer according to contact rates; update adoption state based on weighted masked-neighbor fraction or peer pressure.
  - Initialization and analysis: seed initial mask-wearers, allow layer-specific interventions (e.g., school policy), and measure diffusion metrics across layers.

- Data structure and type:
  - CSV file with one row per agent per day (panel/time-series format). Columns appear to be: day:int, agent_id:int, wearing_mask:bool, received_info:bool.
  - Composite key: (day, agent_id) uniquely identifies a state snapshot.
- Meaning of columns:
  - day: Discrete simulation time step (t = 0, 1, 2, …).
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an agent/node in the social network.
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s behavioral state at that day (true = currently wearing a mask).
  - received_info: Agent’s information state at that day (true = has received mask-related information/encouragement by that day).
- Relationships or nested elements:
  - Flat structure; no nested elements.
  - Temporal relationship: Multiple rows for the same agent across days capture state transitions over time.
  - No social network topology is encoded here (no edges/neighbors); that must be provided/constructed separately.
- How this should inform simulation entities/interactions:
  - Initialize agents: Use day=0 rows to set initial behavior (wearing_mask) and information exposure (received_info) per agent.
  - State variables: Each agent maintains two binary states each timestep—behavior (mask-wearing) and info exposure.
  - Dynamics calibration/validation: If multiple days exist, estimate transition probabilities (e.g., Pr(wear_t+1 | wear_t, info_t)) and validate simulated adoption curves against observed daily aggregates.
  - Interaction logic: In the simulation, received_info should be influenced by network interactions (e.g., info spread from informed neighbors), which then affects the probability of switching to wearing_mask. Since network edges aren’t in this file, integrate an external graph to drive info propagation and peer effects.

model_plan.description: Multi-agent, multiplex-network simulation of mask-wearing behavior diffusion via social influence, policy intervention (from Day 10), information propagation, and market supply constraints. Calibrated on the first 30 days; predicts days 30–39.

modules.name: PolicyEnvironment
modules.description: Activates and updates policy signals (mandate, enforcement, communication, subsidies) from Day 10 onward.

update_rule.pseudocode:
if day >= policy_active_start_day and day <= policy_active_end_day:
  policy_state.mandate_level = mandate_level
  policy_state.enforcement_probability = enforcement_probability
  policy_state.fine_amount = fine_amount
  policy_state.communication_strength = communication_strength
  policy_state.mask_subsidy_level = mask_subsidy_level
else:
  policy_state.mandate_level = 0.0
  policy_state.enforcement_probability = 0.0
  policy_state.fine_amount = 0.0
  policy_state.communication_strength = 0.0
  policy_state.mask_subsidy_level = 0.0
emit(signal.policy_state)
notes: Simple step function policy; can be extended to ramps or time series.
Policy affects both adoption (mandate) and information (communication) and supply (subsidies).

modules.name: InformationDiffusion
modules.description: Updates agents' info_exposure_level via exogenous broadcast and peer social sharing on the multiplex network.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each agent i:
  # Broadcast (exogenous) info
  b = exogenous_info_rate * info_broadcast_reach * info_broadcast_credibility * (1.0 + signal.policy_state.communication_strength)
  # Peer sharing from neighbors who are currently wearing masks (as proxy for sharing pro-mask info)
  peer_family = 1.0 - prod_{j in N_family(i)} (1.0 - share_probability * peer_info_rate_family * 1[state.agent_mask[j]==1])
  peer_work   = 1.0 - prod_{j in N_work(i)}   (1.0 - share_probability * peer_info_rate_work   * 1[state.agent_mask[j]==1])
  peer_comm   = 1.0 - prod_{j in N_comm(i)}   (1.0 - share_probability * peer_info_rate_comm   * 1[state.agent_mask[j]==1])
  peer_total = 1.0 - (1.0 - peer_family)*(1.0 - peer_work)*(1.0 - peer_comm)
  # Decay and update exposure level
  new_info = (1.0 - info_decay_rate) * state.agent_info[i] + b + peer_total
  state.agent_info[i] = min(1.0, max(0.0, new_info))
emit(state.agent_info)
notes: Peer information uses complement-of-products to combine independent transmission channels.
Using mask-wearing neighbors to approximate pro-mask sharing directionally aligns info and behavior.

modules.name: NetworkStats
modules.description: Computes per-layer neighbor mask fractions with observation noise.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each agent i:
  for L in {family, work, community}:
    deg = |N_L(i)|
    frac = 0.0 if deg==0 else (sum_{j in N_L(i)} state.agent_mask[j]) / deg
    noisy_frac = clamp(frac + Normal(0, neighbor_observation_noise_sigma), 0.0, 1.0)
    neighbor_mask_fractions[i][L] = noisy_frac
emit(signal.neighbor_mask_fractions)
notes: Observation noise models imperfect perception of neighbors' behavior.
Edges are treated as undirected simple graphs after preprocessing.

modules.name: SupplyMarket
modules.description: Tracks inventory, sets daily mask price, and fulfills queued orders after a distribution delay.

update_rule.pseudocode:
# Update inventory with production
inventory_level += production_rate_per_day
# Price adjusts toward base with markup during shortages and subsidy reductions
subsidy = signal.policy_state.mask_subsidy_level
effective_base = max(min_mask_price, mask_price_base * (1.0 - subsidy_pass_through * subsidy))
# Compute backlog demand scheduled to be delivered today
deliveries_due_today = pop_orders_from_queue(day)
# Fulfill deliveries due today (inventory reduces now)
allocated_today = min(inventory_level, sum(deliveries_due_today.quantities))
allocation_ratio = 0.0 if sum(deliveries_due_today.quantities)==0 else allocated_today / sum(deliveries_due_today.quantities)
for each order in deliveries_due_today:
  deliver_qty = floor(order.quantity * allocation_ratio)
  emit_delivery(order.agent_id, deliver_qty)
inventory_level -= allocated_today
# Observe new pending orders (placed today) and push to queue with delivery_day = day + distribution_delay_days
for order in signal.pending_orders:
  push_to_queue(delivery_day=day+distribution_delay_days, agent_id=order.agent_id, quantity=order.quantity)
# Update price for tomorrow based on stock tightness
stock_pressure = max(0.0, 1.0 - inventory_level / (production_rate_per_day * (distribution_delay_days + 1)))
mask_price = clamp(effective_base * (1.0 + shortage_markup_beta * stock_pressure), min_mask_price, max_mask_price)
emit(signal.mask_price, mask_price)
emit(signal.deliveries_due_today)
notes: Orders placed today are fulfilled after distribution_delay_days.
Subsidies reduce the effective base price through subsidy_pass_through.
Proportional allocation ensures fairness under shortages.

modules.name: AdoptionDecision
modules.description: Computes adoption intentions, places mask orders, and updates wearing states upon deliveries. Uses logistic adoption with persistence, social influence, information, policy, and cost components.

update_rule.pseudocode:
# 1) Process deliveries arriving today
for each delivery in signal.deliveries_due_today:
  if delivery.quantity > 0:
    state.agent_mask[delivery.agent_id] = 1
    agents[delivery.agent_id].last_adoption_change_day = day
# 2) Compute adoption intentions and place orders
pending_orders = []
for each agent i:
  wear_t = state.agent_mask[i]
  fF = signal.neighbor_mask_fractions[i].family
  fW = signal.neighbor_mask_fractions[i].work
  fC = signal.neighbor_mask_fractions[i].community
  info = state.agent_info[i]
  policy = signal.policy_state.mandate_level
  price = signal.mask_price
  # Weighted peer norm
  peer_term = beta_peer_family * w_family * fF + beta_peer_work * w_work * fW + beta_peer_comm * w_comm * fC
  # Persistence boosts adoption if already wearing
  persistence_term = beta_persistence * wear_t
  # Cost term (negative)
  cost_term = beta_cost * price
  # Policy term (positive)
  policy_term = beta_policy * policy
  # Risk and information effects
  risk_term = beta_risk * agents[i].risk_perception
  info_term = beta_info * info
  # Fatigue reduces propensity over time since last change
  days_since_change = max(0, day - agents[i].last_adoption_change_day)
  fatigue_term = -fatigue_decay_rate * days_since_change
  # Logit score and probability with temperature scaling
  z = beta0_intercept + peer_term + persistence_term + cost_term + policy_term + risk_term + info_term + fatigue_term
  p_adopt = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-z / max(1e-6, noise_temperature)))
  # Bound daily change to avoid oscillations
  if wear_t == 0:
    adopt_prob = min(max_daily_adoption_change, p_adopt)
    will_adopt = Bernoulli(adopt_prob)
    if will_adopt:
      pending_orders.append({agent_id: i, quantity: 1})
  else:
    # Consider disadoption via low propensity (implicit via not placing orders and optionally drop if z very low)
    p_keep = max(p_adopt, 1.0 - max_daily_adoption_change)
    drop = Bernoulli(max(0.0, 1.0 - p_keep))
    if drop:
      state.agent_mask[i] = 0
      agents[i].last_adoption_change_day = day
emit(signal.pending_orders, pending_orders)
emit(state.agent_mask)
notes: Adoption is intention-based with a delivery lag realized via SupplyMarket.
Peer influence is layer-weighted; parameters can be calibrated.
Disadoption occurs when overall propensity is low; constrained to avoid unrealistic churn.

class PolicyEnvironment:
    """
    Encapsulates policy-related parameters and active window for mandates and campaigns.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        mandate_level: float = 0.7,
        enforcement_probability: float = 0.2,
        fine_amount: float = 50.0,
        communication_strength: float = 0.6,
        mask_subsidy_level: float = 0.3,
        active_start_day: int = 10,
        active_end_day: int = 120,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize PolicyEnvironment with specified values.
        """
        self.mandate_level = clamp(float(mandate_level), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.enforcement_probability = clamp(float(enforcement_probability), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.fine_amount = float(fine_amount)
        self.communication_strength = max(0.0, float(communication_strength))
        self.mask_subsidy_level = clamp(float(mask_subsidy_level), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.active_start_day = int(active_start_day)
        self.active_end_day = int(active_end_day)

    def as_state(self, day: int) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Get the current policy state as a dictionary for the given day.
        """
        if self.active_start_day <= day <= self.active_end_day:
            return {
                "mandate_level": self.mandate_level,
                "enforcement_probability": self.enforcement_probability,
                "fine_amount": self.fine_amount,
                "communication_strength": self.communication_strength,
                "mask_subsidy_level": self.mask_subsidy_level,
            }
        else:
            return {
                "mandate_level": 0.0,
                "enforcement_probability": 0.0,
                "fine_amount": 0.0,
                "communication_strength": 0.0,
                "mask_subsidy_level": 0.0,
            }


class SupplyMarket:
    """
    Represents the supply-side market dynamics for mask inventory, pricing, and order fulfillment.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        inventory_level: float = 100000.0,
        production_rate_per_day: float = 10000.0,
        distribution_delay_days: int = 2,
        mask_price: float = 1.0,
        min_mask_price: float = 0.5,
        max_mask_price: float = 3.0,
        mask_price_base: float = 1.0,
        shortage_markup_beta: float = 0.5,
        subsidy_pass_through: float = 0.8,
        price_adjustment_alpha: float = 0.05,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize SupplyMarket with inventory, production, pricing, and delivery parameters.
        """
        self.inventory_level = float(inventory_level)
        self.production_rate_per_day = float(production_rate_per_day)
        self.distribution_delay_days = int(distribution_delay_days)
        self.mask_price = float(mask_price)
        self.min_mask_price = float(min_mask_price)
        self.max_mask_price = float(max_mask_price)
        self.mask_price_base = float(mask_price_base)
        self.shortage_markup_beta = float(shortage_markup_beta)
        self.subsidy_pass_through = clamp(float(subsidy_pass_through), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.price_adjustment_alpha = clamp(float(price_adjustment_alpha), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.pending_orders_queue: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, int]]] = defaultdict(list)

    def push_order(self, agent_id: int, quantity: int, delivery_day: int) -> None:
        """
        Add an order to the delivery queue.
        """
        quantity = max(0, int(quantity))
        if quantity > 0:
            self.pending_orders_queue[int(delivery_day)].append((int(agent_id), quantity))

    def pop_deliveries_due_today(self, day: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
        """
        Retrieve and remove deliveries scheduled for the current day.
        """
        due = self.pending_orders_queue.pop(int(day), [])
        return due

    def update_day(
        self,
        day: int,
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        pending_orders: List[Tuple[int, int]],
    ) -> Tuple[float, List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
        """
        Advance market by one day: produce inventory, deliver due orders proportionally, enqueue new orders, and update price.
        """
        # Production inflow
        self.inventory_level += self.production_rate_per_day

        # Deliveries due today
        deliveries_scheduled = self.pop_deliveries_due_today(day)
        total_due_qty = int(sum(q for _, q in deliveries_scheduled))
        inv_available = int(math.floor(self.inventory_level))
        allocated_today = min(inv_available, total_due_qty)

        deliveries_fulfilled: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        if total_due_qty > 0 and allocated_today > 0:
            # Largest remainder method to ensure sum delivered == allocated_today
            ratio = allocated_today / float(total_due_qty)
            raw_allocs = [qty * ratio for _, qty in deliveries_scheduled]
            floors = [int(math.floor(x)) for x in raw_allocs]
            remainder_units = allocated_today - sum(floors)
            fracs = [(i, raw_allocs[i] - floors[i]) for i in range(len(raw_allocs))]
            fracs.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
            allocs = floors[:]
            for i in range(remainder_units):
                idx = fracs[i][0]
                if deliveries_scheduled[idx][1] > 0:
                    allocs[idx] += 1
            for (agent_id, _), deliver_qty in zip(deliveries_scheduled, allocs):
                if deliver_qty > 0:
                    deliveries_fulfilled.append((agent_id, deliver_qty))
            delivered_sum = sum(q for _, q in deliveries_fulfilled)
        else:
            delivered_sum = 0

        # Reduce inventory by delivered amount
        self.inventory_level -= delivered_sum

        # Price update based on subsidy and stock pressure (target price first)
        subsidy = policy_state.get("mask_subsidy_level", 0.0)
        effective_base = max(self.min_mask_price, self.mask_price_base * (1.0 - self.subsidy_pass_through * subsidy))
        denom = (self.production_rate_per_day * (self.distribution_delay_days + 1))
        stock_pressure = 0.0
        if denom > 0:
            stock_pressure = max(0.0, 1.0 - (self.inventory_level / denom))
        target_price = clamp(effective_base * (1.0 + self.shortage_markup_beta * stock_pressure), self.min_mask_price, self.max_mask_price)
        # Smooth adjustment
        self.mask_price = (1.0 - self.price_adjustment_alpha) * self.mask_price + self.price_adjustment_alpha * target_price

        # Enqueue pending orders for future delivery
        for agent_id, qty in pending_orders:
            self.push_order(agent_id=agent_id, quantity=qty, delivery_day=day + self.distribution_delay_days)

        return float(self.mask_price), deliveries_fulfilled

class NetworkBuilder:
    """
    Builds and validates multiplex network layers (family, work, community) from JSON data or synthetic generation.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def enforce_symmetry(adj: Dict[int, List[int]]) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
        """
        Enforce undirected simple graph symmetry on adjacency lists.
        """
        sym: Dict[int, set] = defaultdict(set)
        for u, nbrs in adj.items():
            for v in nbrs:
                if v == u:
                    continue
                sym[u].add(v)
                sym[v].add(u)
        # Ensure all nodes present
        for u in list(adj.keys()):
            sym.setdefault(u, set())
        return {u: sorted(list(vs)) for u, vs in sym.items()}

    def load_or_build_network(self, agent_ids: List[int], path: str) -> Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]]:
        """
        Load multiplex network layers from JSON file, or build synthetic layers if file is missing or invalid.
        """
        layers = {"family": defaultdict(list), "work": defaultdict(list), "community": defaultdict(list)}
        agent_id_set = set(agent_ids)
        if os.path.exists(path):
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    raw = json.load(f)
                for k, v in raw.items():
                    try:
                        uid = int(k)
                    except Exception:
                        continue
                    if uid not in agent_id_set:
                        continue
                    fam = [int(x) for x in v.get("family", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    work = [int(x) for x in v.get("work_school", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    comm = [int(x) for x in v.get("community", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    layers["family"][uid] = fam
                    layers["work"][uid] = work
                    layers["community"][uid] = comm
                # Enforce symmetry
                for L in ["family", "work", "community"]:
                    layers[L] = self.enforce_symmetry(layers[L])
                # Ensure all agent_ids present
                for aid in agent_ids:
                    for L in ["family", "work", "community"]:
                        layers[L].setdefault(aid, [])
                return layers
            except Exception:
                # Fall back to synthetic
                pass

        # Synthetic small-world-like graphs using networkx Watts-Strogatz for each layer with varying k and p
        n = len(agent_ids)
        if n == 0:
            return {k: {} for k in ["family", "work", "community"]}

        index_to_id = {idx: aid for idx, aid in enumerate(agent_ids)}

        def build_ws(n_nodes: int, k: int, p: float) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
            adj: Dict[int, List[int]] = defaultdict(list)
            if n_nodes < 3:
                # No edges for very small graphs
                for aid in agent_ids:
                    adj.setdefault(aid, [])
                return adj
            k = min(k, n_nodes - 1)
            if k % 2 == 1:
                k -= 1
            if k < 2:
                k = 2
            g = nx.watts_strogatz_graph(n_nodes, k=k, p=clamp(p, 0.0, 1.0), seed=42)
            for u, v in g.edges():
                adj[index_to_id[u]].append(index_to_id[v])
                adj[index_to_id[v]].append(index_to_id[u])
            # enforce symmetry and fill missing nodes
            adj = self.enforce_symmetry(adj)
            for aid in agent_ids:
                adj.setdefault(aid, [])
            return adj

        layers["family"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(6, n - 1)), 0.05)
        layers["work"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(8, n - 1)), 0.1)
        layers["community"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(4, n - 1)), 0.2)
        return layers

class InformationDiffusionModule:
    """
    Module implementing information diffusion via broadcasts and peer sharing across multiplex network.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        exogenous_info_rate: float,
        info_broadcast_credibility: float,
        info_broadcast_reach: float,
        peer_info_rate_family: float,
        peer_info_rate_work: float,
        peer_info_rate_comm: float,
        info_decay_rate: float,
        share_probability: float,
    ) -> None:
        self.exogenous_info_rate = float(exogenous_info_rate)
        self.info_broadcast_credibility = clamp(float(info_broadcast_credibility), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.info_broadcast_reach = clamp(float(info_broadcast_reach), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_family = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_family), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_work = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_work), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_comm = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_comm), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.info_decay_rate = clamp(float(info_decay_rate), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.share_probability = clamp(float(share_probability), 0.0, 1.0)

    def update(
        self,
        agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent],
        info_levels: Dict[int, float],
        mask_state: Dict[int, int],
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        layers: Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]],
    ) -> Dict[int, float]:
        updated = {}
        broadcast_amp = (1.0 + max(0.0, policy_state.get("communication_strength", 0.0)))
        base_broadcast = self.exogenous_info_rate * self.info_broadcast_reach * self.info_broadcast_credibility * broadcast_amp
        for aid in agents.keys():
            # Peer sharing via complement-of-products
            peer_terms = []
            for layer_name, rate in zip(
                ["family", "work", "community"],
                [self.peer_info_rate_family, self.peer_info_rate_work, self.peer_info_rate_comm],
            ):
                prod = 1.0
                for nbr in layers.get(layer_name, {}).get(aid, []):
                    if mask_state.get(nbr, 0) == 1:
                        prod *= (1.0 - self.share_probability * rate)
                peer_term = 1.0 - prod
                peer_terms.append(peer_term)
            peer_total = 1.0 - (1.0 - peer_terms[0]) * (1.0 - peer_terms[1]) * (1.0 - peer_terms[2])
            new_info = (1.0 - self.info_decay_rate) * float(info_levels.get(aid, 0.0)) + base_broadcast + peer_total

    def __init__(

    ) -> None:

        self.beta_persistence = float(beta_persistence)
        self.fatigue_decay_rate = max(0.0, float(fatigue_decay_rate))
        self.noise_temperature = max(1e-6, float(noise_temperature))
        self.w_family = clamp(float(w_family), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.w_work = clamp(float(w_work), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.w_comm = clamp(float(w_comm), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.max_daily_adoption_change = clamp(float(max_daily_adoption_change), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.rng = rng

    def update(
        self,
        day: int,
        agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent],
        mask_state: Dict[int, int],
        info_levels: Dict[int, float],
        neighbor_mask_fractions: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]],
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        mask_price: float,
        deliveries_due_today: List[Tuple[int, int]],
    ) -> Tuple[Dict[int, int], List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
        # Process deliveries to set mask state to 1
        for agent_id, delivered_qty in deliveries_due_today:
            if delivered_qty > 0:
                mask_state[agent_id] = 1
                agents[agent_id].last_adoption_change_day = day

        pending_orders: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []

        for aid, agent in agents.items():
            wear_t = int(mask_state.get(aid, 0))
            frac_family = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("family", 0.0)
            frac_work = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("work", 0.0)
            frac_comm = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("community", 0.0)
            info = float(info_levels.get(aid, 0.0))
            policy = float(policy_state.get("mandate_level", 0.0))
            price = float(mask_price)

            # Expected penalty for non-compliance (applies when not wearing)
            enforcement_probability = float(policy_state.get("enforcement_probability", 0.0))
            fine_amount = float(policy_state.get("fine_amount", 0.0))
            expected_penalty = enforcement_probability * fine_amount
            # Treat penalty as reducing the "effective cost" of adopting (since not adopting is costly)
            effective_cost = price - (expected_penalty if wear_t == 0 else 0.0)

            peer_term = (
                self.beta_peer_family * self.w_family * frac_family
                + self.beta_peer_work * self.w_work * frac_work
                + self.beta_peer_comm * self.w_comm * frac_comm
            )
            persistence_term = self.beta_persistence * wear_t
            cost_term = self.beta_cost * effective_cost
            policy_term = self.beta_policy * policy
            risk_term = self.beta_risk * agent.risk_perception
            info_term = self.beta_info * info
            days_since_change = max(0, day - agent.last_adoption_change_day)
            fatigue_term = -self.fatigue_decay_rate * days_since_change

            z = self.beta0 + peer_term + persistence_term + cost_term + policy_term + risk_term + info_term + fatigue_term
            p_adopt = logistic(z, self.noise_temperature)

            if wear_t == 0:
                adopt_prob = min(self.max_daily_adoption_change, p_adopt)
                if self.rng.random() < adopt_prob:
                    pending_orders.append((aid, 1))
            else:
                p_keep = max(p_adopt, 1.0 - self.max_daily_adoption_change)
                drop_prob = max(0.0, 1.0 - p_keep)
                if self.rng.random() < drop_prob:
                    mask_state[aid] = 0
                    agent.last_adoption_change_day = day

        return mask_state, pending_orders

class Metrics:
    """
    Implements evaluation metrics for simulated adoption time series.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def rmse(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        err = np.array(y_true[:n]) - np.array(y_pred[:n])
        return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(err ** 2)))

    @staticmethod
    def mae(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        err = np.abs(np.array(y_true[:n]) - np.array(y_pred[:n]))
        return float(np.mean(err))

    @staticmethod
    def r2(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        yt = np.array(y_true[:n])
        yp = np.array(y_pred[:n])
        ss_res = np.sum((yt - yp) ** 2)
        ss_tot = np.sum((yt - yt.mean()) ** 2)
        if ss_tot == 0.0:
            return float("nan")
        return float(1.0 - (ss_res / ss_tot))

    @staticmethod
    def peak_timing_error(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        t_peak = int(np.argmax(y_true[:n]))
        p_peak = int(np.argmax(y_pred[:n]))
        return float(abs(t_peak - p_peak))

    @staticmethod
    def final_gap(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        return float(abs(y_true[n - 1] - y_pred[n - 1]))

            self.state['agent_info'] = self.modules['info'].update(

                info_levels=self.state['agent_info'],
                mask_state=self.state['agent_mask'],
                policy_state=policy_state,
                layers=self.layers,
            )

                agents=self.agents,
                mask_state=self.state['agent_mask'],
                layers=self.layers,
            )

def clamp(x: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
    """
    Clamp a numeric value between lower and upper bounds.
    """
    return max(lo, min(hi, x))


def bernoulli(p: float) -> bool:
    """
    Draw a Bernoulli random variable.
    """
    p = clamp(p, 0.0, 1.0)
    return random.random() < p


def logistic(z: float, temperature: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """
    Temperature-scaled logistic function.
    """
    t = max(1e-6, float(temperature))
    try:
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-z / t))
    except OverflowError:
        if z > 0:
            return 1.0
        else:

    def as_state(self, day: int) -> Dict[str, float]:

class SupplyMarket:
    """
    Represents the supply-side market dynamics for mask inventory, pricing, and order fulfillment.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        inventory_level: float = 100000.0,
        production_rate_per_day: float = 10000.0,
        distribution_delay_days: int = 2,
        mask_price: float = 1.0,
        min_mask_price: float = 0.5,
        max_mask_price: float = 3.0,
        mask_price_base: float = 1.0,
        shortage_markup_beta: float = 0.5,
        subsidy_pass_through: float = 0.8,
        price_adjustment_alpha: float = 0.05,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize SupplyMarket with inventory, production, pricing, and delivery parameters.
        """
        self.inventory_level = float(inventory_level)
        self.production_rate_per_day = float(production_rate_per_day)
        self.distribution_delay_days = int(distribution_delay_days)
        self.mask_price = float(mask_price)
        self.min_mask_price = float(min_mask_price)
        self.max_mask_price = float(max_mask_price)
        self.mask_price_base = float(mask_price_base)
        self.shortage_markup_beta = float(shortage_markup_beta)
        self.subsidy_pass_through = clamp(float(subsidy_pass_through), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.price_adjustment_alpha = clamp(float(price_adjustment_alpha), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.pending_orders_queue: Dict[int, List[Tuple[int, int]]] = defaultdict(list)

    def push_order(self, agent_id: int, quantity: int, delivery_day: int) -> None:
        """
        Add an order to the delivery queue.
        """
        quantity = max(0, int(quantity))
        if quantity > 0:
            self.pending_orders_queue[int(delivery_day)].append((int(agent_id), quantity))

    def pop_deliveries_due_today(self, day: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
        """
        Retrieve and remove deliveries scheduled for the current day.
        """
        due = self.pending_orders_queue.pop(int(day), [])
        return due

    def update_day(
        self,
        day: int,
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        pending_orders: List[Tuple[int, int]],
    ) -> Tuple[float, List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
        """
        Advance market by one day: produce inventory, deliver due orders proportionally, enqueue new orders, and update price.
        """
        # Production inflow
        self.inventory_level += self.production_rate_per_day

        # Deliveries due today
        deliveries_scheduled = self.pop_deliveries_due_today(day)
        total_due_qty = int(sum(q for _, q in deliveries_scheduled))
        inv_available = int(math.floor(self.inventory_level))
        allocated_today = min(inv_available, total_due_qty)

        deliveries_fulfilled: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        if total_due_qty > 0 and allocated_today > 0:
            # Largest remainder method to ensure sum delivered == allocated_today
            ratio = allocated_today / float(total_due_qty)
            raw_allocs = [qty * ratio for _, qty in deliveries_scheduled]
            floors = [int(math.floor(x)) for x in raw_allocs]
            remainder_units = allocated_today - sum(floors)
            fracs = [(i, raw_allocs[i] - floors[i]) for i in range(len(raw_allocs))]
            fracs.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
            allocs = floors[:]
            for i in range(remainder_units):
                idx = fracs[i][0]
                if deliveries_scheduled[idx][1] > 0:
                    allocs[idx] += 1
            for (agent_id, _), deliver_qty in zip(deliveries_scheduled, allocs):
                if deliver_qty > 0:
                    deliveries_fulfilled.append((agent_id, deliver_qty))
            delivered_sum = sum(q for _, q in deliveries_fulfilled)
        else:
            delivered_sum = 0

        # Reduce inventory by delivered amount
        self.inventory_level -= delivered_sum

        # Price update based on subsidy and stock pressure (target price first)
        subsidy = policy_state.get("mask_subsidy_level", 0.0)
        effective_base = max(self.min_mask_price, self.mask_price_base * (1.0 - self.subsidy_pass_through * subsidy))
        denom = (self.production_rate_per_day * (self.distribution_delay_days + 1))
        stock_pressure = 0.0
        if denom > 0:
            stock_pressure = max(0.0, 1.0 - (self.inventory_level / denom))
        target_price = clamp(effective_base * (1.0 + self.shortage_markup_beta * stock_pressure), self.min_mask_price, self.max_mask_price)
        # Smooth adjustment
        self.mask_price = (1.0 - self.price_adjustment_alpha) * self.mask_price + self.price_adjustment_alpha * target_price

        # Enqueue pending orders for future delivery
        for agent_id, qty in pending_orders:
            self.push_order(agent_id=agent_id, quantity=qty, delivery_day=day + self.distribution_delay_days)

        return float(self.mask_price), deliveries_fulfilled

class NetworkBuilder:
    """
    Builds and validates multiplex network layers (family, work, community) from JSON data or synthetic generation.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def enforce_symmetry(adj: Dict[int, List[int]]) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
        """
        Enforce undirected simple graph symmetry on adjacency lists.
        """
        sym: Dict[int, set] = defaultdict(set)
        for u, nbrs in adj.items():
            for v in nbrs:
                if v == u:
                    continue
                sym[u].add(v)
                sym[v].add(u)
        # Ensure all nodes present
        for u in list(adj.keys()):
            sym.setdefault(u, set())
        return {u: sorted(list(vs)) for u, vs in sym.items()}

    def load_or_build_network(self, agent_ids: List[int], path: str) -> Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]]:
        """
        Load multiplex network layers from JSON file, or build synthetic layers if file is missing or invalid.
        """
        layers = {"family": defaultdict(list), "work": defaultdict(list), "community": defaultdict(list)}
        agent_id_set = set(agent_ids)
        if os.path.exists(path):
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    raw = json.load(f)
                for k, v in raw.items():
                    try:
                        uid = int(k)
                    except Exception:
                        continue
                    if uid not in agent_id_set:
                        continue
                    fam = [int(x) for x in v.get("family", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    work = [int(x) for x in v.get("work_school", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    comm = [int(x) for x in v.get("community", []) if int(x) in agent_id_set and int(x) != uid]
                    layers["family"][uid] = fam
                    layers["work"][uid] = work
                    layers["community"][uid] = comm
                # Enforce symmetry
                for L in ["family", "work", "community"]:
                    layers[L] = self.enforce_symmetry(layers[L])
                # Ensure all agent_ids present
                for aid in agent_ids:
                    for L in ["family", "work", "community"]:
                        layers[L].setdefault(aid, [])
                return layers
            except Exception:
                # Fall back to synthetic
                pass

        # Synthetic small-world-like graphs using networkx Watts-Strogatz for each layer with varying k and p
        n = len(agent_ids)
        if n == 0:
            return {k: {} for k in ["family", "work", "community"]}

        index_to_id = {idx: aid for idx, aid in enumerate(agent_ids)}

        def build_ws(n_nodes: int, k: int, p: float) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
            adj: Dict[int, List[int]] = defaultdict(list)
            if n_nodes < 3:
                # No edges for very small graphs
                for aid in agent_ids:
                    adj.setdefault(aid, [])
                return adj
            k = min(k, n_nodes - 1)
            if k % 2 == 1:
                k -= 1
            if k < 2:
                k = 2
            g = nx.watts_strogatz_graph(n_nodes, k=k, p=clamp(p, 0.0, 1.0), seed=42)
            for u, v in g.edges():
                adj[index_to_id[u]].append(index_to_id[v])
                adj[index_to_id[v]].append(index_to_id[u])
            # enforce symmetry and fill missing nodes
            adj = self.enforce_symmetry(adj)
            for aid in agent_ids:
                adj.setdefault(aid, [])
            return adj

        layers["family"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(6, n - 1)), 0.05)
        layers["work"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(8, n - 1)), 0.1)
        layers["community"] = build_ws(n, max(2, min(4, n - 1)), 0.2)
        return layers

class InformationDiffusionModule:
    """
    Module implementing information diffusion via broadcasts and peer sharing across multiplex network.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        exogenous_info_rate: float,
        info_broadcast_credibility: float,
        info_broadcast_reach: float,
        peer_info_rate_family: float,
        peer_info_rate_work: float,
        peer_info_rate_comm: float,
        info_decay_rate: float,
        share_probability: float,
    ) -> None:
        self.exogenous_info_rate = float(exogenous_info_rate)
        self.info_broadcast_credibility = clamp(float(info_broadcast_credibility), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.info_broadcast_reach = clamp(float(info_broadcast_reach), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_family = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_family), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_work = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_work), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.peer_info_rate_comm = clamp(float(peer_info_rate_comm), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.info_decay_rate = clamp(float(info_decay_rate), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.share_probability = clamp(float(share_probability), 0.0, 1.0)

    def update(
        self,
        agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent],
        info_levels: Dict[int, float],
        mask_state: Dict[int, int],
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        layers: Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]],
    ) -> Dict[int, float]:
        updated = {}
        broadcast_amp = (1.0 + max(0.0, policy_state.get("communication_strength", 0.0)))
        base_broadcast = self.exogenous_info_rate * self.info_broadcast_reach * self.info_broadcast_credibility * broadcast_amp
        for aid in agents.keys():
            # Peer sharing via complement-of-products
            peer_terms = []
            for layer_name, rate in zip(
                ["family", "work", "community"],
                [self.peer_info_rate_family, self.peer_info_rate_work, self.peer_info_rate_comm],
            ):
                prod = 1.0
                for nbr in layers.get(layer_name, {}).get(aid, []):
                    if mask_state.get(nbr, 0) == 1:
                        prod *= (1.0 - self.share_probability * rate)
                peer_term = 1.0 - prod
                peer_terms.append(peer_term)
            peer_total = 1.0 - (1.0 - peer_terms[0]) * (1.0 - peer_terms[1]) * (1.0 - peer_terms[2])
            new_info = (1.0 - self.info_decay_rate) * float(info_levels.get(aid, 0.0)) + base_broadcast + peer_total
            updated[aid] = clamp(new_info, 0.0, 1.0)
        return updated


class NetworkStatsModule:
    """
    Module that computes neighbor mask fractions per layer with observation noise.
    """

    def __init__(self, neighbor_observation_noise_sigma: float, rng: np.random.Generator) -> None:
        self.noise_sigma = max(0.0, float(neighbor_observation_noise_sigma))
        self.rng = rng

    def update(
        self,
        agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent],
        mask_state: Dict[int, int],
        layers: Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]],
    ) -> Dict[int, Dict[str, float]]:
        out: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]] = {}
        for aid in agents.keys():
            per_layer = {}
            for L in ["family", "work", "community"]:
                nbrs = layers.get(L, {}).get(aid, [])
                deg = len(nbrs)
                frac = 0.0
                if deg > 0:
                    frac = sum(mask_state.get(nbr, 0) for nbr in nbrs) / float(deg)
                noisy = clamp(frac + float(self.rng.normal(0.0, self.noise_sigma)), 0.0, 1.0)
                per_layer[L] = noisy
            out[aid] = per_layer
        return out


class AdoptionDecisionModule:
    """
    Module that computes adoption decisions, places orders, and handles deliveries.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        beta0_intercept: float,
        beta_peer_family: float,
        beta_peer_work: float,
        beta_peer_comm: float,
        beta_info: float,
        beta_risk: float,
        beta_policy: float,
        beta_cost: float,
        beta_persistence: float,
        fatigue_decay_rate: float,
        noise_temperature: float,
        w_family: float,
        w_work: float,
        w_comm: float,
        max_daily_adoption_change: float,
        rng: np.random.Generator,
    ) -> None:
        self.beta0 = float(beta0_intercept)
        self.beta_peer_family = float(beta_peer_family)
        self.beta_peer_work = float(beta_peer_work)
        self.beta_peer_comm = float(beta_peer_comm)
        self.beta_info = float(beta_info)
        self.beta_risk = float(beta_risk)
        self.beta_policy = float(beta_policy)
        self.beta_cost = float(beta_cost)
        self.beta_persistence = float(beta_persistence)
        self.fatigue_decay_rate = max(0.0, float(fatigue_decay_rate))
        self.noise_temperature = max(1e-6, float(noise_temperature))
        self.w_family = clamp(float(w_family), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.w_work = clamp(float(w_work), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.w_comm = clamp(float(w_comm), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.max_daily_adoption_change = clamp(float(max_daily_adoption_change), 0.0, 1.0)
        self.rng = rng

    def update(
        self,
        day: int,
        agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent],
        mask_state: Dict[int, int],
        info_levels: Dict[int, float],
        neighbor_mask_fractions: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]],
        policy_state: Dict[str, float],
        mask_price: float,
        deliveries_due_today: List[Tuple[int, int]],
    ) -> Tuple[Dict[int, int], List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
        # Process deliveries to set mask state to 1
        for agent_id, delivered_qty in deliveries_due_today:
            if delivered_qty > 0:
                mask_state[agent_id] = 1
                agents[agent_id].last_adoption_change_day = day

        pending_orders: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []

        for aid, agent in agents.items():
            wear_t = int(mask_state.get(aid, 0))
            frac_family = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("family", 0.0)
            frac_work = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("work", 0.0)
            frac_comm = neighbor_mask_fractions.get(aid, {}).get("community", 0.0)
            info = float(info_levels.get(aid, 0.0))
            policy = float(policy_state.get("mandate_level", 0.0))
            price = float(mask_price)

            # Expected penalty for non-compliance (applies when not wearing)
            enforcement_probability = float(policy_state.get("enforcement_probability", 0.0))
            fine_amount = float(policy_state.get("fine_amount", 0.0))
            expected_penalty = enforcement_probability * fine_amount
            # Treat penalty as reducing the "effective cost" of adopting (since not adopting is costly)
            effective_cost = price - (expected_penalty if wear_t == 0 else 0.0)

            peer_term = (
                self.beta_peer_family * self.w_family * frac_family
                + self.beta_peer_work * self.w_work * frac_work
                + self.beta_peer_comm * self.w_comm * frac_comm
            )
            persistence_term = self.beta_persistence * wear_t
            cost_term = self.beta_cost * effective_cost
            policy_term = self.beta_policy * policy
            risk_term = self.beta_risk * agent.risk_perception
            info_term = self.beta_info * info
            days_since_change = max(0, day - agent.last_adoption_change_day)
            fatigue_term = -self.fatigue_decay_rate * days_since_change

            z = self.beta0 + peer_term + persistence_term + cost_term + policy_term + risk_term + info_term + fatigue_term
            p_adopt = logistic(z, self.noise_temperature)

            if wear_t == 0:
                adopt_prob = min(self.max_daily_adoption_change, p_adopt)
                if self.rng.random() < adopt_prob:
                    pending_orders.append((aid, 1))
            else:
                p_keep = max(p_adopt, 1.0 - self.max_daily_adoption_change)
                drop_prob = max(0.0, 1.0 - p_keep)
                if self.rng.random() < drop_prob:
                    mask_state[aid] = 0
                    agent.last_adoption_change_day = day

        return mask_state, pending_orders


class AdoptionAggregatorModule:
    """
    Module that aggregates daily adoption into a single observable timeseries.
    """

    def __init__(self, smoothing_window_days: int = 1) -> None:
        self.window = max(1, int(smoothing_window_days))
        self.history: Deque[float] = deque(maxlen=self.window)

    def update(self, mask_state: Dict[int, int]) -> float:
        total = len(mask_state)
        rate = 0.0
        if total > 0:
            rate = sum(mask_state.values()) / float(total)
        self.history.append(rate)
        return float(np.mean(self.history)) if self.window > 1 else rate


class Metrics:
    """
    Implements evaluation metrics for simulated adoption time series.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def rmse(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        err = np.array(y_true[:n]) - np.array(y_pred[:n])
        return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(err ** 2)))

    @staticmethod
    def mae(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        err = np.abs(np.array(y_true[:n]) - np.array(y_pred[:n]))
        return float(np.mean(err))

    @staticmethod
    def r2(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        yt = np.array(y_true[:n])
        yp = np.array(y_pred[:n])
        ss_res = np.sum((yt - yp) ** 2)
        ss_tot = np.sum((yt - yt.mean()) ** 2)
        if ss_tot == 0.0:
            return float("nan")
        return float(1.0 - (ss_res / ss_tot))

    @staticmethod
    def peak_timing_error(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        t_peak = int(np.argmax(y_true[:n]))
        p_peak = int(np.argmax(y_pred[:n]))
        return float(abs(t_peak - p_peak))

    @staticmethod
    def final_gap(y_true: List[float], y_pred: List[float]) -> float:
        n = min(len(y_true), len(y_pred))
        if n == 0:
            return float("nan")
        return float(abs(y_true[n - 1] - y_pred[n - 1]))

class Simulation:
    """
    Coordinates and runs the multi-agent simulation according to the model plan.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_plan: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.model_plan = model_plan
        self.config: Dict[str, Any] = self._extract_parameters(model_plan)
        seed = int(self.config.get("seed", 42))
        random.seed(seed)
        np.random.seed(seed)
        self.rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(seed)

        # Containers
        self.agents: Dict[int, PersonAgent] = {}
        self.layers: Dict[str, Dict[int, List[int]]] = {"family": {}, "work": {}, "community": {}}
        self.policy_env: Optional[PolicyEnvironment] = None
        self.market: Optional[SupplyMarket] = None
        self.info_source: Optional[InformationSource] = None
        self.modules: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.state: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "agent_mask": {},
            "agent_info": {},
        }
        self.results: Dict[str, List[Any]] = {
            "day": [],
            "observable.adoption_rate_daily": [],
            "mask_price": [],
        }
        self.observed_adoption: List[float] = []

        # Paths to data
        self.agent_file = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "agent_attributes.csv")
        self.network_file = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "social_network.json")
        self.train_file = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "train_data.csv")

        # Initialize environment and state
        self._initialize_entities_and_data()

    def _extract_parameters(self, model_plan: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Flatten parameter list in the model plan into a simple dict of key -> default value.
        """
        params = {}
        for p in model_plan.get("parameters", []):
